feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector leadership: clear positioning, relevant scope, and good evidence of progression and ownership. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline and summary align well with the experience and establish a focused niche in digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Strong credibility through progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement supports leadership claims and shows increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale and outcomes: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” add impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition and structure: “Topline Skills,” “Core Competencies,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to reduce redundancy and improve scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, or performance where possible.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation and bullet formatting are inconsistent; “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically uneven; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak filler. No obvious misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector positioning. It reads polished, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and recent roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and make the value proposition more outcome-oriented; consider “digital platforms and operating models” instead of the longer list.
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “multi-channel platforms serving millions annually.”
- Reduce list density in sentence two by grouping related areas: “web modernization, analytics, editorial governance, and multimedia/AI-enabled experiences.”
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building and modernizing digital platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Enterprise web modernization” and “editorial systems” are repeated elsewhere, so avoid adding more detail in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and phrased with sharper parallel structure.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, cleaner competency labels with consistent noun phrasing; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “Multi-channel communications operations” with “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Consider changing “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI search and content discovery” for brevity and clarity.
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of “&” if the rest of the CV favors a more formal tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps heavily with the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid repeating tool-specific language already covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already strongly established in the header and work history.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce your web, campaign, and multimedia range, but the block is dense and overlaps with achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and making formatting more scannable would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add bullets and parallel structure: start each item with a strong verb + outcome focus.
- Tighten wording and remove filler like “designed for continued campaign growth” unless you can quantify scale or results.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “bill-level,” and spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.
- Consider a sharper version: “Recent Projects: AI-enabled legislative search; Drupal 10 campaign microsite; anniversary storytelling campaign with interactive conference display; recurring advocacy video series across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially repeat current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most additive item; keep it if space is limited.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground outcomes/ownership, and avoid repeating project details already covered in Recent Projects and earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a sharper value statement: “Lead digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets starting with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Advised,” “Developed,” “Improved.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, toolkit downloads, or engagement gains.
- Example rewrite: “Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including modular microsites, member toolkits, and front-end enhancements for large public-facing web properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video series already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance, analytics, and multi-channel operations overlap with NACo roles; emphasize new consulting ownership and current enterprise improvements.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with solid platform metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad opener with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization as the anchor bullet: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, reporting cadence, production volume, or efficiency gains from governance/analytics improvements.
- Tighten channel bullet to emphasize strategy/scale, not routine management: “Oversaw email and social strategy reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video growth and recurring advocacy programming overlap with the prior NACo roles; here, focus on building the in-house studio as the step-change.
- “Strengthened governance/publishing workflows” echoes earlier entries; quantify operational improvement if possible.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story within NACo, but this entry overlaps heavily with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Tighten it to emphasize scope growth, team coordination, and channel ownership at this stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show level-up in responsibility: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and sharpen outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and distinct: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague workflow language with clearer operational impact: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” closely overlap with the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video updates also appear in the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on scaling/owning the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance rather than repeating generic communications terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations and publishing standards
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing “leadership,” “messaging,” and “planning” styles.
- Consider swapping “multi-channel” for “cross-channel” or “enterprise” to sound more senior and distinct.
- If space allows elsewhere, move proof of impact to experience bullets rather than skills (e.g., 10,000+ page migration, 50+ publishers, tens of thousands reached).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent strengths rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a list of tools to a tighter capability statement, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-priority or older platform mentions here unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages from this topline item.
- Cut “jQuery” from Topline Skills; it reads dated and is better left in Technical + IT if needed.
- Use broader, impact-oriented phrasing like “enterprise CMS modernization” and “search and discovery experiences” to align with recent consulting and director-level work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools for a senior digital leader, but this item reads like a generic software list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize strategic analytics leadership over tool inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and KPI framework design
- Executive and leadership reporting dashboards
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- SEO, user behavior analysis and performance optimization
- Put strategy first, tools second; “KPI design” and “leadership reporting” are stronger signals than listing platforms first.
- Consider replacing “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX insight and conversion/performance analysis” if accurate.
- Keep to 4 bullets max for scanability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization.”
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; this section should signal senior capability, while Technical + IT can hold the full stack.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both “Core Competencies” and multiple NACo experience bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery scope, e.g.:
- Broadcast-quality studio production
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production systems
- Video editing and post-production
- Virtual event and webcast operations
- Put the strongest, most distinctive capability first: “Broadcast-quality studio production” or “Livestream and hybrid event delivery.”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrasing like “Video editing and post-production” if studio build/event delivery is the bigger differentiator.
- If space allows, align wording with proven experience: “In-house studio operations” or “Advocacy and event video production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove one instance.
- “Studio operations” echoes the NACo bullet about building an in-house studio, so keep this section concise rather than repeating impact.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to actual use: “Drupal (migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping the title repetition by renaming to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace the weakest/least relevant item with a stronger technical differentiator already evidenced elsewhere only if not duplicated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, and CMS modernization.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus your enterprise-level experience unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools tied to recent delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End Development & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, REST/API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in brief parentheticals: Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting), GitHub Actions (deployment automation), GTM (tracking implementation)
- Consider dropping version numbers unless used consistently elsewhere: HTML, CSS, JavaScript is cleaner than HTML5/CSS3

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation”; avoid repeating automation language across both sections

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation/integration tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-value or older/general items unless directly used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If accurate, add a qualifier to show applied impact: **Workflow automation, intake tracking, approvals, and cross-team coordination**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack/Teams overlap with standard workplace tools; keep only if they support a workflow/operations narrative rather than basic communication.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for this profile, but the line is too bare and misses the scale/leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations rather than read like a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parenthetical form: **Higher Logic (member communications/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- Keep it platform-focused; let work experience carry outcomes like audience size and newsletter volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in Director/Associate Director entries.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere, so keep this item specifically about email/CRM platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is mostly a keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods most tied to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Analytics & Optimization Tools
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboards
- Replace broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” with more specific tools or outputs; “Google Search Console” and “KPI dashboards” read sharper.
- If accurate, consider adding one higher-signal capability instead of a generic term: conversion analysis, funnel reporting, or experimentation design.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is very close to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one section or making this one tools-only and the other outcomes/capabilities.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, add 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video content; and coordinated day-to-day digital publishing and production.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: number of livestreams, frequency of video updates, audience size, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or omit if supervision was informal.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on launching/building the capability, not scaling it.
- “Strengthening workflows” is repeated across multiple roles; distinguish this as early team formation and foundational process setup.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with more active wording such as “produced multimedia and digital content assets for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Consider a two-part structure: research/program support first, then podcast/multimedia ownership second.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support and the first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads more like a mixed skills/activities list than a clean tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets, so tighten it to software/platform proficiency only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or refocus as tools only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep production capabilities here, make them more specific and concise: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast editing”
- Use consistent category logic: software in this section; operational capabilities in “Topline Skills” or experience bullets.
- If proficiency is strong, consider adding level only where meaningful: “Premiere Pro (advanced)” rather than listing generic creative tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream studio workflows” duplicates “Livestreaming • PTZ camera systems • Studio operations • Hybrid and virtual event production.”
- “Podcast production” is already supported by older experience; keep only if still central to current positioning.
